content.question: Who founded the Mughal Empire in 1526?
content.note: Babur, a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan, founded the Mughal Empire after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

content.question: Who wrote Ain-i-Akbari?
content.note: Abul Fazl, one of the 'Nine Gems' of Akbar's court, wrote the Ain-i-Akbari. It is the third volume of the Akbarnama and details the administration and statistics of Akbar's empire.

content.question: Who defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain?
content.note: In 1192 CE, Muhammad Ghori defeated the Rajput king Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain, which opened the doors for Muslim rule in North India.

content.question: Who defeated Humayun at Chausa and Kannauj?
content.note: The Afghan leader Sher Shah Suri defeated the Mughal Emperor Humayun at the Battle of Chausa (1539) and the Battle of Kannauj (1540), forcing Humayun into exile for 15 years.

content.question: Who wrote Kitab-ul-Hind?
content.note: The Persian scholar Al-Biruni accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind, an encyclopedic work on Indian philosophy, religion, and culture.

content.question: Who attacked the Somnath temple in 1026 CE?
content.note: Mahmud of Ghazni, the ruler of the Ghaznavid Empire, conducted 17 raids on India. His 16th raid in 1026 CE targeted the wealthy Somnath Temple in Gujarat.

content.question: Who was the first Muslim woman ruler of Delhi?
content.note: Razia Sultan, the daughter of Iltutmish, was the first and only female sovereign to rule the Delhi Sultanate (1236–1240).

content.question: Who introduced Din-i-Ilahi?
content.note: Akbar introduced Din-i-Ilahi ('Divine Faith') in 1582 CE. It was a syncretic religion intended to merge the best elements of various faiths to promote national unity.

content.question: Who founded the Vijayanagara Empire?
content.note: The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 CE by two brothers, Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, on the banks of the Tungabhadra River in South India.

content.question: Who invaded India in 712 CE?
content.note: The Umayyad Caliphate's general Muhammad bin Qasim invaded and conquered the Sindh region in 712 CE, marking the first major Arab conquest in India.

content.question: Who was Akbar’s guardian?
content.note: Bairam Khan served as the military commander and guardian for the young Akbar. He led the Mughal forces to victory in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).

content.question: Which Mughal ruler re-imposed Jizya tax?
content.note: Aurangzeb, known for his orthodox religious policies, re-imposed the Jizya tax (a tax on non-Muslim subjects) in 1679, which had been previously abolished by Akbar.

content.question: What was the major industry during the Mughal period?
content.note: During the Mughal era, Cotton textiles were the backbone of India's economy. Indian calicos and muslins were in high demand globally, particularly in Europe and Southeast Asia.

content.question: Who defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526?
content.note: Babur, the ruler of Kabul, defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of the Lodi Dynasty. Babur's success is attributed to his superior cavalry and the first significant use of gunpowder and artillery in Indian warfare.

content.question: In which year did Timur invade Delhi?
content.note: In 1398 CE, the Turco-Mongol conqueror Timur (Tamerlane) invaded Delhi, severely weakening the Tughlaq Dynasty. His invasion left the city in ruins and paved the way for future Central Asian conquests.

content.question: When was the Battle of Khanwa fought?
content.note: The Battle of Khanwa was fought in 1527 CE between Babur and the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga of Mewar. Babur's victory consolidated Mughal power in Northern India.

content.question: Who defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain (1191 CE)?
content.note: Prithviraj Chauhan, the ruler of the Chauhan dynasty, defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain. However, Ghori returned a year later to win the second battle, changing the course of Indian history.

content.question: Who were considered successors of Timur?
content.note: The Mughals considered themselves the direct successors of Timur. Babur, the founder of the empire, was a paternal descendant of Timur and a maternal descendant of Genghis Khan.

content.question: The Battle of Haldighati was fought between whom?
content.note: Fought in 1576, the Battle of Haldighati was a fierce conflict between the forces of Mughal Emperor Akbar (led by Man Singh I) and Maharana Pratap of Mewar. Although the Mughals won, Pratap continued his resistance from the hills.

content.question: Who founded the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara Empire?
content.note: Veer Narasimha founded the Tuluva Dynasty in 1505 CE. This dynasty produced the most famous ruler of Vijayanagara, Krishnadevaraya, under whom the empire reached its zenith.

content.question: Which was the last dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire?
content.note: The Aravidu Dynasty was the fourth and final dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire. It was founded by Tirumala Deva Raya after the empire was severely weakened in the Battle of Talikota (1565).

content.question: In which year was the First Battle of Tarain fought?
content.note: The First Battle of Tarain occurred in 1191 CE near Karnal. It was a rare instance where an Indian king, Prithviraj Chauhan, decisively repelled a foreign Islamic invader in open combat.

content.question: Which famous monument is a replica of the Taj Mahal built in 1679?
content.note: Bibi Ka Maqbara, located in Aurangabad, was commissioned by Aurangzeb in memory of his wife Dilras Banu Begum. It is often called the 'Taj of the Deccan' due to its striking resemblance to the original Taj Mahal.

content.question: Tansen was a musician in the court of which Mughal emperor?
content.note: Tansen, the legendary singer and composer, was one of the Navaratnas (Nine Gems) in the court of Akbar. He is credited with creating many ragas, including Mian Ki Malhar.

content.question: In which language did Babur write Tuzuk-i-Baburi?
content.note: Babur wrote his autobiography, Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama), in Turki (Chagatai Turkic). It is considered one of the most honest and detailed memoirs of any medieval monarch.

content.question: What was the road built by Sher Shah Suri called?
content.note: The Grand Trunk Road (GT Road) was rebuilt and extended by Sher Shah Suri to connect Sonargaon (Bangladesh) with Kabul (Afghanistan), facilitating trade and communication across the subcontinent.

content.question: Who developed Akbar's revenue system Zabt?
content.note: Raja Todarmal, Akbar's finance minister, developed the Zabt or Dahshala system. It was an efficient land revenue system based on the average yield and prices of the previous ten years.
